preprint.title: Critical mixing in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model

review.locator_convention: Preprint locations use the compiled numbering and page numbers of paper.pdf. Source locators refer to the version identified by the source's arXiv id or DOI.

category.A: Unattributed reuse: a technique, construction, identity, estimate or body of theory from an identifiable earlier paper is reused without credit for that content.
category.B: Same-problem precedence: earlier, uncited partial progress on the same problem, such as a weaker or special-case version of a statement the preprint proves.
category.C: Structural: a published result would replace or substantially shorten a large part of the argument.

grade.Strong: (A/B) The earlier technique is reused essentially intact without credit for that content.
grade.Partial: (A/B) Only a fragment is reused, or the credit is present but only indirect.
grade.Major: (C) A route, a section, or a component of the main theorem becomes a citation.
grade.Moderate: (C) A multi-page chain of lemmas becomes a citation.

source_status.not_cited: The work is not in the preprint's bibliography.
source_status.cited_for_other_content: The work is in the preprint's bibliography but is not cited for this content.
source_status.credited_in_part: The preprint cites the work for part of this content only.
source_status.credited_elsewhere: The preprint cites the work for this content at other locations, but not where the content is used.
source_status.credited_indirectly: The preprint cites a location (e.g. a companion lemma) that itself credits the work for this content.

findings.technique: El Alaoui–Montanari–Sellke planted stochastic-localization framework for SK
findings.summary: The preprint studies the SK Gibbs measure inside the EAMS framework: a Gaussian observation of a Gibbs sample, the TAP equation with the observation as field, and the planted law with its likelihood transfer to ordinary disorder.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Not cited. A companion credits EAMS for this combination, in a passage the preprint does not cite.

sources.role: Gaussian observation process, TAP equation at the observation field, planted law and likelihood transfer

findings.summary: The curvature inequality behind route 1's terminal spectral gap is Wang's signed two-spin estimate summed over pairs, imported through a companion lemma.
findings.credit_in_preprint: Indirectly, via a companion lemma that credits Wang. The preprint's own citation of Wang is for his β<1/2 mixing theorem.

sources.locators: Lemma 3.4 and proof of Thm. 1.2, pp. 10–13
sources.role: signed two-spin curvature estimate and its summation over pairs

findings.technique: Critical-temperature bounds on the SK partition function and covariance
findings.summary: Earlier versions exist of the partition-function lower bound (7.5) (stronger), the covariance lower bound (7.6) (weaker), and the bottom-scale covariance bound (12.8) (only an s=0, ordinary-law analogue with log n).
findings.credit_in_preprint: (7.5) indirectly, via Du–Huang's Theorem 1.6; otherwise not cited.

sources.role: free-energy CLT and critical overlap bound

findings.technique: Log-Sobolev constant from the support profile (Hermon–Peres characterization)
findings.summary: The support profile at the end of route 1 already gives the log-Sobolev exponent by the Hermon–Peres characterization, so the spectral-cap route is not needed for Theorem 1.1.
findings.impact: About 70 pages (§§15–19) become unnecessary for Theorem 1.1.
